context.requirement_text:
Second half of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix for its own stated PRIMARY
surface, atop REQ-216's core module. Mirrors REQ-186/REQ-187's and
REQ-214/REQ-215's own "core module first, wiring requirement(s)
second, disjoint files" split precedent in this file.

TWO ADMISSION GATES, NOT ONE, because tenant identity is not known
until partway through `Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline`'s existing chain --
read in full (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex): `Plug.Parsers` runs
first, then `assign_trace_id`, then `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(which itself resolves tenant identity via a DB read -- token
verification, tenant-by-realm/slug resolution, JIT provisioning --
i.e. AuthPipeline's OWN work already consumes a DB connection BEFORE
any tenant identity exists to gate on), then
`Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`, then `match`/`dispatch`. Given that
ordering, a single per-tenant-only gate cannot run early enough to
cover AuthPipeline's own connection use. Resolved as follows, stated
as an accepted, disclosed limitation rather than silently glossed
over (matching this project's own honesty convention for a limitation
that cannot be fully closed within one requirement's scope, e.g.
decision 0014's own disclosed WASM native-crash gap):

1. GLOBAL gate, mounted FIRST in the chain -- before `Plug.Parsers`,
so a request rejected for lack of capacity is rejected before any
body-parsing work is spent on it. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)`. Covers AuthPipeline's own
connection use (the gap named above) because it runs before
AuthPipeline and gates ALL downstream DB-connection-holding work,
auth included.
2. PER-TENANT gate, mounted immediately AFTER `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(tenant identity now resolved into `conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id`)
and BEFORE `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`/`match`/`dispatch`. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, schema_name})`, resolving
`schema_name` the same way `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus` and
`Letflow.Scheduler.Poller` already do (tenant-id -> schema-name
resolution already exists in this codebase; reuse it, do not
re-derive). Covers TenantStatus's own DB lookup and every sub-router's
dispatch work -- the dominant share of connection-holding time per
REQ-056/ISS-0431's own round-trip profiling.
DISCLOSED LIMITATION: AuthPipeline's own DB work (steps 1-4 of its
moduledoc) is covered by the global gate only, not a per-tenant one,
because tenant identity does not exist yet at that point in the
chain. This is accepted, not silently omitted -- state it in this
plug's own moduledoc.
3. Both gates: on `{:error, :capacity}`, respond immediately (halt the
plug chain, no further plugs run) via
`Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2` (REQ-066, ALREADY
EXISTING -- do not add a new response helper), with the
`Retry-After` header set explicitly on the conn first (matching
`Response.rate_limited/2`'s own documented "caller sets Retry-After"
convention) to a fixed, configured seconds value (config, default 1)
-- NOT a computed estimate, since this admission mechanism has no
queueing/backoff-timing model to estimate from (a fixed short value
matching `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`'s own existing `@retry_after_seconds
"30"` precedent's SHAPE, though the specific number here is
independently justified: admission rejection is a near-instant
decision with no wait queue behind it, unlike TenantStatus's
migration-in-progress case, so a MUCH shorter retry-after is
appropriate -- state this reasoning in the plug's moduledoc rather
than copying TenantStatus's 30-second value uncritically).
4. On success at BOTH gates: the plug stores both `admission_ref()`s
in `conn.assigns` and registers a `Plug.Conn.register_before_send/2`
(or equivalent, matching how this codebase already threads
request-scoped cleanup -- state which mechanism is chosen and why) or
calls `Letflow.Admission.release/1` for both refs when the response is
sent, so an admitted request's slot is freed exactly once, on every
response path including a request that raises inside a downstream
plug or router (verified in the acceptance criteria below).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore logic;
no change to `Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit` (still deferred, unmounted,
unrelated mechanism); no Poller wiring (REQ-218); no tier-weighted
per-tenant caps (REQ-216's own recorded open question).

result.summary:
Ran `mix letflow.check.test` (source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh first) in the foreground on branch feature/WF02-REQ217-20260903 at commit 483e3c845987fdd9ea0316abc12d85f658da0236, against docker-compose Postgres/Keycloak already running on the .env-pinned port (LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5463). Waited synchronously for the real result (process ran 1397.1 seconds / ~23.3 minutes; no result was fabricated or assumed).

REAL QUOTED OUTPUT (final lines of the run):
```
Finished in 1397.1 seconds (15.6s async, 1381.5s sync)

Result: 3080/3096 passed (6/6 properties, 3074/3090 tests), 10 excluded
Failed: 16 tests
...
** (Mix) mix letflow.check.test: FAILED -- underlying `mix test` run exited 2 (real test failure/error).
[exited with code 1]
```

DIAGNOSIS OF ALL 16 FAILURES (each read individually from the real output, not summarized from memory):

(a) KNOWN PRE-EXISTING RUSTC-ENOENT FLAKE -- 2 of 16: `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest` 'a mismatched rust pin reports a MISMATCH row...' and 'a matching rust pin reports OK with no mismatch', both failing with `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"], ...)`. Confirmed directly: `which rustc` on this host exits 1 (no rustc installed). Exactly the documented, known limitation.

(c, ruled out) NOT connected to this branch's files -- 14 of 16: failures in `Letflow.SandboxPoolTest` (1), `Letflow.ServiceCatalogTest` (4), `Letflow.TenantSchemaReaperTest` (3), `Letflow.ServiceCatalogReaperTest` (3), `Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest` (1), `Letflow.Scheduler.PollerTest` (2). None of these reference or exercise `lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex`, `lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex`, or `lib/letflow/admission.ex` -- confirmed by reading every failure's full stacktrace; none touch those modules. `git diff --stat main...HEAD -- lib/` for this branch shows exactly 3 changed files: the REQ-217 design doc, `lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex`, and `lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex` -- no other lib/ file was touched, so these 14 failing modules (sandbox pooling, service-catalog scope/reaping, tenant-schema reaping, identity-table migration guard, scheduler poller) are structurally unreachable from this branch's changes. All 14 failures are timing/race-shaped assertions against shared, concurrently-mutated global state (schema-name-set snapshots mid-teardown, `:sys.get_state/1` against a possibly-already-exited GenServer PID, concurrent-invocation liveness guards, a Postgrex connection disconnect mid-query) -- the classic signature of order-/timing-dependent flakiness under full non-partitioned concurrent `mix test`, not deterministic logic bugs.

ZERO failures in `test/letflow/plugs/admission_test.exs` or `test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs` (REQ-217's own test files) -- grepped the full failure list explicitly; confirmed by absence.

FLAKINESS CONFIRMED BY RE-RUN (not just asserted): re-ran the 6 failing modules in isolation (`mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs test/letflow/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs test/letflow/service_catalog_reaper_test.exs test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs`), foreground, real output:
```
Finished in 55.7 seconds (0.00s async, 55.7s sync)

Result: 75 passed
```
All 75 tests in the previously-failing modules passed cleanly with no shared-state contention from the rest of the suite -- directly demonstrating the 14 failures are environment-timing-dependent under full-suite concurrent load, not a deterministic regression, and reinforced by TEST-DESIGNER's own prior full-suite run on this same branch (step-07 handoff) reporting only 2 failures (the same rustc pair) at 3094/3096 -- the 14 additional failures seen on this run did not reproduce on that earlier run of the identical code, which is itself evidence against a deterministic regression in this branch's diff.

NET ASSESSMENT: no genuine new regression connected to `lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex`, `lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex`, or `lib/letflow/admission.ex` was found. All 16 failures are accounted for: 2 are the documented pre-existing rustc-toolchain flake (category a), 14 are pre-existing, order-/timing-dependent flaky tests in subsystems this branch never touches, confirmed non-reproducing in isolation (75/75) and not seen on this same branch's prior full-suite run. Recommending PASS to Step 5; RELEASE-VALIDATOR should independently re-run per its own mandate and may see a different subset of the 14 flaky failures (or none) given their timing-dependent nature -- this is expected and does not indicate this report is wrong.
